findings.failure_mode: Metrics are attributed to the wrong store, corrupting observability of the mode-3 rollout

findings.root_cause: The error branch of the new Mode3 Create copies the legacy-duration recorder while measuring the storage call (startStorage)
findings.suggested_fix: Call d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) in the storage error branch of Create
findings.title: Storage-failure duration in Create recorded under the legacy metric

findings.body: Failed unified-storage updates are counted in the legacy duration histogram with is_error=true, hiding storage update failures from storage-side metrics and inflating legacy error rates

findings.impact: Failed unified-storage updates are counted in the legacy duration histogram with is_error=true, hiding storage update failures from storage-side metrics and inflating legacy error rates

findings.suggested_fix: Replace with d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) in the Update storage-error branch
findings.title: Storage-failure duration in Update recorded under the legacy metric

findings.body: The legacy DeleteCollection duration and error outcome are observed in the storage histogram, so legacy delete-collection failures are invisible in legacy metrics and storage metrics are double-counted for this method

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection duration recorded as storage duration in async goroutine

findings.verifier_reason: Line R166 verbatim shows `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` inside the goroutine measuring `startLegacy`. This records legacy duration under the storage histogram, inverse of candidates 0/1.

findings.body: The 'kind' label of grafana_dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds is populated with per-object names, causing unbounded label cardinality and making successful deletes unaggregatable with the error path (which uses options.Kind)
findings.failure_mode: High-cardinality, inconsistent metric labels degrade Prometheus performance and break queries grouping by kind
findings.impact: The 'kind' label of grafana_dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds is populated with per-object names, causing unbounded label cardinality and making successful deletes unaggregatable with the error path (which uses options.Kind)
findings.root_cause: Wrong variable passed as the kind label in the new Delete implementation (error path at R103 correctly uses options.Kind)
findings.suggested_fix: Pass options.Kind instead of name to recordStorageDuration on the success path of Delete
findings.title: Delete success metric uses object name instead of kind as the 'kind' label
findings.trigger: Every successful Mode3 Delete request; each distinct object name creates a new metric series
findings.verifier_reason: Line R106 verbatim shows `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` where `name` (object name) is passed as the kind label. Error path at R103 correctly uses `options.Kind`, causing inconsistent high-cardinality labels.

pr.body:
**What is this feature?**

Mode 3 will work the following way:

reads (get, list) : only use unified storage
writes (create, update, delete, delete-collection) : write to unified storage and then asynchronously, write to legacy, just as a safe measure.

**Why do we need this feature?**

[Add a description of the problem the feature is trying to solve.]

**Who is this feature for?**

[Add information on what kind of user the feature is for.]

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

Fixes https://github.com/grafana/search-and-storage-team/issues/53

raw_findings.body: Log lines emitted by downstream storage/legacy code lose the name, kind, and method key-values that were just computed, unlike every other Mode3 method which passes the enriched 'log' variable
raw_findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent, less diagnosable logs for delete operations
raw_findings.impact: Log lines emitted by downstream storage/legacy code lose the name, kind, and method key-values that were just computed, unlike every other Mode3 method which passes the enriched 'log' variable
raw_findings.root_cause: The local enriched logger variable 'log' is built but d.Log is passed to klog.NewContext in Delete
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Change to ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, log) to match Create/Get/List/Update/DeleteCollection
raw_findings.title: Delete stores the unenriched logger d.Log in the context instead of the request-scoped log
raw_findings.trigger: Any Mode3 Delete request; downstream code retrieving the logger via klog.FromContext(ctx)

raw_findings.body: The background legacy write races against request-context cancellation and will frequently fail with 'context canceled' before completing, so the 'write to legacy as a safe measure' silently does not happen and the two stores diverge; the failure is only visible as a metric, never surfaced to the caller
raw_findings.evidence: ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, errors.New("legacy create timeout"))
raw_findings.failure_mode: Legacy storage misses writes nondeterministically, defeating the dual-write guarantee of Mode3
raw_findings.impact: The background legacy write races against request-context cancellation and will frequently fail with 'context canceled' before completing, so the 'write to legacy as a safe measure' silently does not happen and the two stores diverge; the failure is only visible as a metric, never surfaced to the caller
raw_findings.root_cause: The goroutine's timeout context is a child of the incoming request ctx, whose cancellation propagates to the async legacy call after the response is sent
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Detach the goroutine context from the request context (e.g. context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or context.Background() carrying over only values/logger) before applying the 10s timeout; same fix needed at lines 110, 135, and 163
raw_findings.title: Async legacy writes derive their context from the request context, which is canceled when the handler returns
raw_findings.trigger: Any Mode3 Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection: the method returns to the apiserver handler immediately after spawning the goroutine, and the apiserver cancels the per-request context when the response is written

raw_findings.body: objInfo.UpdatedObject/Preconditions are re-evaluated against the legacy old object with a storage-derived resourceVersion, so the legacy update can fail with a conflict or produce a different object than what was written to storage, silently diverging the two stores (mode1/mode2 wrap the result in updateWrapper for exactly this reason)
raw_findings.evidence: _, _, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, createValidation, updateValidation, forceAllowCreate, options)
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent legacy-side update failures or divergent content between legacy and unified storage
raw_findings.impact: objInfo.UpdatedObject/Preconditions are re-evaluated against the legacy old object with a storage-derived resourceVersion, so the legacy update can fail with a conflict or produce a different object than what was written to storage, silently diverging the two stores (mode1/mode2 wrap the result in updateWrapper for exactly this reason)
raw_findings.root_cause: The rewrite dropped the updateWrapper indirection that ensured the same resolved object was written to both stores
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the object returned by d.Storage.Update in an updateWrapper (objInfo = &updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: res.DeepCopyObject()}) before calling d.Legacy.Update, as done in the other dual-writer modes
raw_findings.title: Legacy Update in the goroutine reuses the raw objInfo instead of wrapping the object already persisted to storage
raw_findings.trigger: A Mode3 Update where the client-supplied objInfo carries resourceVersion preconditions or patch semantics computed against unified storage (whose resource versions differ from legacy SQL versions), or where objInfo is not safe to re-evaluate concurrently after the request completes

validated_findings.body: The 'kind' label of grafana_dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds is populated with per-object names, causing unbounded label cardinality and making successful deletes unaggregatable with the error path (which uses options.Kind)
validated_findings.failure_mode: High-cardinality, inconsistent metric labels degrade Prometheus performance and break queries grouping by kind
validated_findings.impact: The 'kind' label of grafana_dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds is populated with per-object names, causing unbounded label cardinality and making successful deletes unaggregatable with the error path (which uses options.Kind)
validated_findings.root_cause: Wrong variable passed as the kind label in the new Delete implementation (error path at R103 correctly uses options.Kind)
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass options.Kind instead of name to recordStorageDuration on the success path of Delete
validated_findings.title: Delete success metric uses object name instead of kind as the 'kind' label
validated_findings.trigger: Every successful Mode3 Delete request; each distinct object name creates a new metric series
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R106 verbatim shows `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` where `name` (object name) is passed as the kind label. Error path at R103 correctly uses `options.Kind`, causing inconsistent high-cardinality labels.

validated_findings.body: Log lines emitted by downstream storage/legacy code lose the name, kind, and method key-values that were just computed, unlike every other Mode3 method which passes the enriched 'log' variable
validated_findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent, less diagnosable logs for delete operations
validated_findings.impact: Log lines emitted by downstream storage/legacy code lose the name, kind, and method key-values that were just computed, unlike every other Mode3 method which passes the enriched 'log' variable
validated_findings.root_cause: The local enriched logger variable 'log' is built but d.Log is passed to klog.NewContext in Delete
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Change to ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, log) to match Create/Get/List/Update/DeleteCollection
validated_findings.title: Delete stores the unenriched logger d.Log in the context instead of the request-scoped log
validated_findings.trigger: Any Mode3 Delete request; downstream code retrieving the logger via klog.FromContext(ctx)
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R97 verbatim shows `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` while the enriched `log` variable is defined at R96. Other methods pass `log` to NewContext. This causes downstream logs to lose name/kind/method context.

validated_findings.body: The background legacy write races against request-context cancellation and will frequently fail with 'context canceled' before completing, so the 'write to legacy as a safe measure' silently does not happen and the two stores diverge; the failure is only visible as a metric, never surfaced to the caller
validated_findings.evidence: ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, errors.New("legacy create timeout"))
validated_findings.failure_mode: Legacy storage misses writes nondeterministically, defeating the dual-write guarantee of Mode3
validated_findings.impact: The background legacy write races against request-context cancellation and will frequently fail with 'context canceled' before completing, so the 'write to legacy as a safe measure' silently does not happen and the two stores diverge; the failure is only visible as a metric, never surfaced to the caller
validated_findings.root_cause: The goroutine's timeout context is a child of the incoming request ctx, whose cancellation propagates to the async legacy call after the response is sent
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Detach the goroutine context from the request context (e.g. context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or context.Background() carrying over only values/logger) before applying the 10s timeout; same fix needed at lines 110, 135, and 163
validated_findings.title: Async legacy writes derive their context from the request context, which is canceled when the handler returns
validated_findings.trigger: Any Mode3 Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection: the method returns to the apiserver handler immediately after spawning the goroutine, and the apiserver cancels the per-request context when the response is written
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that request context cancellation propagates to the goroutine is speculative. The patch shows `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` which creates a child context, but whether the parent is canceled when the handler returns depends on apiserver behavior not evidenced here. The 10s timeout may complete before cancellation in typical cases.

validated_findings.body: objInfo.UpdatedObject/Preconditions are re-evaluated against the legacy old object with a storage-derived resourceVersion, so the legacy update can fail with a conflict or produce a different object than what was written to storage, silently diverging the two stores (mode1/mode2 wrap the result in updateWrapper for exactly this reason)
validated_findings.evidence: _, _, errObjectSt := d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, createValidation, updateValidation, forceAllowCreate, options)
validated_findings.failure_mode: Silent legacy-side update failures or divergent content between legacy and unified storage
validated_findings.impact: objInfo.UpdatedObject/Preconditions are re-evaluated against the legacy old object with a storage-derived resourceVersion, so the legacy update can fail with a conflict or produce a different object than what was written to storage, silently diverging the two stores (mode1/mode2 wrap the result in updateWrapper for exactly this reason)
validated_findings.root_cause: The rewrite dropped the updateWrapper indirection that ensured the same resolved object was written to both stores
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the object returned by d.Storage.Update in an updateWrapper (objInfo = &updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: res.DeepCopyObject()}) before calling d.Legacy.Update, as done in the other dual-writer modes
validated_findings.title: Legacy Update in the goroutine reuses the raw objInfo instead of wrapping the object already persisted to storage
validated_findings.trigger: A Mode3 Update where the client-supplied objInfo carries resourceVersion preconditions or patch semantics computed against unified storage (whose resource versions differ from legacy SQL versions), or where objInfo is not safe to re-evaluate concurrently after the request completes
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R139 verbatim shows `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` passing raw `objInfo` instead of wrapping the storage result. Mode1/Mode2 use `updateWrapper` to ensure the same resolved object is written to both stores. This can cause divergence when objInfo re-evaluates against legacy's different resourceVersion.

validated_findings.body: testify's mock panics ('I don't know what to return') inside the background goroutine, crashing the whole test binary nondeterministically depending on whether the goroutine runs before the process exits (flaky CI failures)
validated_findings.evidence: obj, _, err := dw.Delete(context.Background(), tt.input, func(ctx context.Context, obj runtime.Object) error { return nil }, &metav1.DeleteOptions{})
validated_findings.failure_mode: Flaky panic-driven test failures that are hard to attribute
validated_findings.impact: testify's mock panics ('I don't know what to return') inside the background goroutine, crashing the whole test binary nondeterministically depending on whether the goroutine runs before the process exits (flaky CI failures)
validated_findings.root_cause: The new test only stubs the storage mock even though the code under test now also calls the legacy store asynchronously
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a setupLegacyFn registering m.On("Delete", ...) for the success case (and synchronize on the goroutine, e.g. via the mock expectation), mirroring the storage setup
validated_findings.title: TestMode3_Delete sets no legacy mock expectation while Delete asynchronously calls Legacy.Delete
validated_findings.trigger: Running TestMode3_Delete's success case: DualWriterMode3.Delete spawns a goroutine that invokes d.Legacy.Delete, which hits legacyStoreMock's m.Called with no registered 'Delete' expectation
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Test at R230 calls `dw.Delete` which spawns a goroutine calling `d.Legacy.Delete`. The test only sets up `setupStorageFn` with no legacy mock expectation. testify mock will panic on unexpected calls, causing flaky test failures.
